clauses.prior_judgment_reason: Clause sec2-c ('(c) Within 45 days of the date of this order, the head of each agency with agency actions described in subsection (a) of this section shall develop and submit to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB Director) ...'). The time period in this clause is a report or action deadline, not an end: the order has no wording that terminates the clause when the report or action is done, and a performed command stays part of the order until it is revoked (AGENT_PROTOCOL step 3). The producer does not claim the date any report was delivered; that date is not an end-date source. First end = EO 13990 sec. 7(a) revocation, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. The 45-day plan date is a deadline, not an end.
clauses.required_scope_review: The second sentence provides no further responsibilities under section 2 after a qualifying written no-actions statement, absent a contrary OMB determination. Obtain each relevant statement and OMB response; do not assume the condition occurred.

finding: The blanket assertion that the order has no termination condition overlooks the express agency-specific release in section 2(c). The source itself makes a qualifying no-actions statement and the absence of a contrary OMB determination material. Actual agency statements and report completion dates have not been established in this audit.
limitations: All five original EOs were read in their held extracted-text representation. Original PDF pages were not visually inspected in this audit; source locations remain subject to page verification.
Only the explicitly listed pages of the two newly acquired PDFs were visually inspected. No claim to a complete page-image reading is made.
No exact completion date is inferred from a deadline, publication bound or a later revocation.
No agency-specific completion/exemption/nonperformance fact is inferred from silence in a by-number EO search.
This is a targeted audit of one material premise and related source contradictions, not certification of every clause, later event, savings state or current predicate.
